# Video script: Which mode, for which question

> DRAFT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE. Contains claims with status 'ai-extracted' that no clinician has verified.

Unit F1 | Target length: 6 min

| # | Shot | Narration | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Presenter to camera | We will compare the modes by what each is used for. Structure, flow, velocity, timing. | - |
| 2 | Machine console: preset and mode keys | Two-dimensional imaging. Narrow the sector, and keep the frame rate above thirty to forty hertz. | AS23-007 |
| 3 | Four-chamber clip, grey-scale then colour side by side | Colour shows that blood flows, and which way. Set the scale to the velocities of interest. | AS23-009, AS23-010, IS23-041 |
| 4 | Pulmonary vein on colour, then power Doppler | For small vessels and slow flow, power Doppler helps. | AS23-011 |
| 5 | Screen capture: sample gate placed on a valve, spectral trace below | Pulsed-wave Doppler gives the flow pattern at one point. Line up with the flow, angle below twenty degrees. Small gate. | AS23-012 |
| 6 | M-mode trace with atrial and ventricular walls labelled | For rhythm, M-mode through an atrial wall and a ventricular free wall shows which contracts when. | AS23-017 |
| 7 | Screen: thermal and mechanical index display | Keep exposure as low as reasonably achievable. Be aware of the indices. In early pregnancy keep them at one or below. | AS23-005, AS23-006 |
